entities.name: PMID:10744933
observations: Pooled retrospective audit from 22 UK breast units included 8,783 women with significant family history and 9,075 woman-years of follow-up.
Screen-detected tumors had more favorable pathological features; no observed mortality endpoint or randomized comparison was reported.
Authors concluded screening appeared effective and expected a survival benefit.

entities.name: PMID:21093374
observations: Prospective single-arm FH01 study enrolled 6,710 women at intermediate familial risk receiving annual mammography.
Among 136 cancers, 77% were screen-detected; invasive cancers were smaller, less node-positive, and lower grade than comparison controls.
Projected, not observed, 10-year mortality favored surveillance: 1.10% versus 1.38%, adjusted relative risk 0.80 (95% CI 0.66–0.96).

entities.name: PMID:23489892
observations: FH01 HTA evaluation included 6,710 women aged mainly 40–49 with at least 3% breast-cancer risk during ages 40–49 and annual mammography.
Among 165 cancers, 74% were screen-detected; modeled mortality reduction was 40% with RR 0.60 (95% CI 0.37–0.98), but mortality was not directly observed in a randomized trial.

entities.name: Familial screening evidence
observations: Annual mammographic surveillance appears beneficial for carefully risk-defined women under 50 with significant or moderate familial risk.

Evidence supports favorable detection and tumor characteristics, but mortality benefit remains observational and model-based, with possible lead-time, length-time, selection, and comparison-group biases.
